title: Without foreknowledge of free acts God would not be omniscient
source_text: VIII. Et certe si Deus ab aeterno futura quaelibet non praescit, sed ignorat ea quae sunt a creaturis libere agenda, omniscientia Deo amplius tribuenda non est; neque vere dici potest omnia scire, siquidem nonnulla sunt quae latent ejus scientiam.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly if God does not foreknow from eternity any future things whatever, but is ignorant of those things which are to be done freely by creatures, omniscience is no longer to be attributed to God; nor can he truly be said to know all things, since there are some things which lie hidden from his knowledge.
pass_b_english: Certainly, if God does not know every future thing from eternity, but is ignorant of what creatures will freely do, omniscience can no longer be ascribed to him.
Nor can he truly be said to know all things, since some things would be hidden from his knowledge.

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
